I also traced the callers of the changed functions: `review-fix-queue.ts`'s `upsertReviewFinding`/`recordReviewFinding` usage, `webhook.ts`'s `recordReviewFinding` import, `review-process.ts`'s `fixer` field (to confirm the repository-fix process never runs AI-Implement's own fix pass and so is correctly untouched by the `closedKeys` exemption), and `dedup.ts`'s schema (confirmed `review_findings.status` has no `CHECK` constraint, so the new `'rejected'` value needs no migration). **Summary of the change:** an `invalid` disposition now behaves like `follow-up` for gating purposes — the runner-callback persists it as a new `rejected` ledger status (`markReviewFindingsRejectedByKeys`), which (like `deferred`) survives re-reports of the same finding key (`upsertReviewFinding`'s `CASE WHEN` and `recordReviewFinding`'s early-return both updated), is excluded from `listOpenReviewFindings`, and is accepted by `LateExternalReview`'s fail-closed check alongside `deferred`. In `post-push-review.ts`, a `closedKeys` set (renamed from `deferredKeys`) now also absorbs `invalid` keys, so a repeated external finding with the same key no longer re-gates merge readiness or reappears in the fix prompt, and a `rejectedFindingsByKey` map renders a cumulative "Rejected by the fix pass" block on every terminal/fix-pass PR comment. `replyToDispositionThreads` now also resolves the GitHub thread on an `invalid` disposition (previously it replied but left it open). I traced the full data flow end to end — review-ledger upsert/resolve semantics, the runner-callback ordering (rejections and deferrals are applied before any outcome/phase branch, consistent with the AII-756 pattern), every one of the 12 `postPrComment` call sites in `post-push-review.ts` (all correctly append `rejectedCommentBlock()` from the point dispositions can exist onward), and the `LateExternalReview` fail-closed logic — and didn't find a correctness bug. Test coverage is thorough: it covers thread resolution ordering (reply must succeed before resolve), summary-only findings (no thread mutation), repeated-key vs. new-key reporting on the next head, cross-cycle retention of multiple rejections, and the DB-level re-report/reopen semantics. The docs (`docs/review-fix-rail.md`) were updated in matching detail, and the integration recipe gives a reasonable manual end-to-end check. Two minor, non-blocking observations: 1. **`src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts` (`rejectedCommentBlock`, ~line 2026):** the posted "Rejected by the fix pass" PR comment renders the raw 64-character SHA-256 `findingKey` to a human reader (`` `- Finding \`${d.findingKey}\`: ${d.reason}` ``), whereas the directly analogous human-facing comment for the sibling `follow-up` disposition, `renderDeferredFindingsComment` (`src/runner-callback.ts:1495`), looks up the stored finding row and renders `source · path:line — reason (url)` instead. The hash is not meaningful to a PR reader; it would be more consistent (and more useful) to look the row up the same way. This is intentional and covered by tests (`expect(terminal).toContain(findingKey)`), so it's a style/readability nit rather than a defect. 2. **`docs/adr/028-the-fixing-agent-dispositions-each-finding-and-may-defer-out-of-scope-ones.md`:** this PR is a real policy change to the behavior the ADR documents — previously "`invalid` is not filtered — it stays gating so the next review decides" (the old doc text), now an `invalid` disposition permanently closes the finding the same way `follow-up`/`deferred` does, plus a new ledger status (`rejected`). `docs/review-fix-rail.md` was updated thoroughly and even cites "ADR 028 decision 4" for the new rule, but ADR 028's own decision 4 text still only mentions `follow-up`/`deferred`, not `invalid`/`rejected` — so the citation now points at a decision that doesn't contain what it's cited for. This exact ADR already has an "Amendment (2026-10-28)" section recording a similarly-scoped extension of the `deferred` rule to the verdict level; following that same pattern with a new amendment for the `rejected` extension would keep the ADR a trustworthy source instead of a stale one. Neither finding blocks merge.

## Claude review

**Verdict:** approve

Reviewed PR #1541 (AII-1813), which makes an `invalid` fix-pass disposition behave like `follow-up` for merge-gating purposes: it is now persisted as a new `rejected` ledger status (alongside `open`/`resolved`/`deferred`) that survives re-reports of the same finding key, is excluded from open-findings reads, is accepted by LateExternalReview's fail-closed check, and causes the review thread to be resolved (not just replied to). post-push-review.ts tracks these in a `closedKeys` set (renamed from `deferredKeys`) that also now exempts the external-verdict-blocks gate when every listed finding is closed, and renders a cumulative "Rejected by the fix pass" block on PR comments via a new `rejectedFindingsByKey` map.

Files read in full: docs/review-fix-rail.md, integration-tests/recipes/rejected-review-finding.md, src/__tests__/finding-dispositions.test.ts, src/__tests__/late-external-review.test.ts, src/__tests__/post-push-review.test.ts, src/__tests__/review-ledger-store.test.ts, src/__tests__/runner-callback.test.ts, src/pipeline/finding-dispositions.ts, src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts, src/restate/late-external-review.ts, src/review-ledger-store.ts, src/runner-callback.ts. I also traced callers/consumers not in the diff: review-fix-queue.ts's and webhook.ts's use of upsertReviewFinding/recordReviewFinding, review-process.ts's `fixer` field (confirming the repository-fix process -- which never runs AI-Implement's own fix pass -- is correctly untouched by the closedKeys exemption), and dedup.ts's schema (confirming review_findings.status has no CHECK constraint, so the new 'rejected' value needs no migration).

I verified: the DB upsert/record-finding CASE logic correctly treats 'rejected' like 'deferred' (never reopened by a repeat report, but a genuinely different body still produces a new open row); runner-callback.ts applies rejections unconditionally before any outcome/phase branch (mirroring the existing AII-756 follow-up pattern) and no longer double-resolves invalid-disposed findings via the gap-analysis snapshot path; all 12 postPrComment call sites in post-push-review.ts that occur after dispositions can exist correctly append the new rejected-comment block, while the few earlier ones (where it would always be empty) correctly don't; LateExternalReview's fail-closed check was correctly extended to accept 'rejected' alongside 'deferred'; and replyToDispositionThreads now resolves the thread on 'invalid' only after a successful reply (tested). Test coverage is thorough, covering thread-resolution ordering, summary-only findings with no thread mutation, repeated vs. new findings on a later head, cross-cycle retention of multiple rejections, and DB-level reopen semantics. Documentation (docs/review-fix-rail.md) was updated in matching detail and the new integration recipe is reasonable.

I found no correctness bugs. Two minor, non-blocking issues: (1) the new PR-facing "Rejected by the fix pass" comment shows the raw SHA-256 findingKey rather than a human-readable origin, unlike the analogous renderDeferredFindingsComment; (2) ADR 028 documents the old "invalid stays gating" policy and was not amended even though review-fix-rail.md now cites "ADR 028 decision 4" for the new rule that decision's text doesn't actually contain, despite this exact ADR already having a precedent "Amendment" section for a similarly-scoped extension.

This makes the comment much less useful to a person reviewing the PR, though it is intentional and covered by tests asserting the raw key appears.

The same ADR already has an `Amendment (2026-10-28)` section for an equivalent-scope extension of the `deferred` rule, so following that established pattern here would keep the ADR accurate rather than stale.

## Claude review

**Verdict:** changes_requested

Read the full diff (origin/ai-implement/feature/aii-1811...HEAD) and every changed file in full: docs/review-fix-rail.md, integration-tests/recipes/rejected-review-finding.md, src/__tests__/finding-dispositions.test.ts, src/__tests__/late-external-review.test.ts, src/__tests__/post-push-review.test.ts, src/__tests__/review-ledger-store.test.ts, src/__tests__/runner-callback.test.ts, src/pipeline/finding-dispositions.ts, src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts, src/restate/late-external-review.ts, src/review-ledger-store.ts, src/runner-callback.ts. Also traced callers/consumers: review-fix-queue.ts and webhook.ts (no reference to the review_findings status enum, unaffected by the new `rejected` value), and dedup.ts's schema (confirmed no CHECK constraint on `review_findings.status`, so `rejected` needs no migration).

This is a fix-pass commit ("fix: address review feedback (iter 1)") responding to a prior blocking finding: the verdict-exception logic (`minorOnlyContractFindings`/`minorOnlyProcessFindings`) previously required *every* listed finding to be minor, so a repeated rejected blocker mixed with an undisposed minor finding still blocked approval. The fix replaces both checks with a single `allFindingsNonBlockingOrClosed` helper that accepts a finding if it is either `minor` severity or its key is in the (renamed) `closedKeys` set — I traced this through both the `review-contract` (`contractFindings`) and non-default-process (`processVerdict.findings`) paths and verified the gating math is correct for the reported scenario, including the "empty findings still blocks" and "an open/non-closed blocking finding still blocks" cases. Three new parameterized tests (`post-push-review.test.ts`) exercise exactly this scenario across both `ai-implement` and `claude-code-review` processes, plus retention across fix cycles and summary-only (no-thread) findings — I checked the test fixtures' `stableReviewFindingKey` construction matches the production finding shapes.

The rest of the ledger/callback/late-review machinery (persisting `invalid` as a new `rejected` status, `upsertReviewFinding`'s CASE WHEN, `recordReviewFinding`'s early return, `markReviewFindingsRejectedByKeys`, the runner-callback's unconditional-before-phase-branch rejection write mirroring the AII-756 follow-up pattern, `replyToDispositionThreads` now resolving the thread after a successful `invalid` reply, and `LateExternalReview`'s fail-closed check accepting `deferred` or `rejected`) all read correctly and are covered by the corresponding unit tests I inspected in each test file's diff.

I found no bug that reopens or blocks incorrectly in the core gating logic the fix pass targeted. I did find one new, verifiable gap introduced by this PR's own "Rejected by the fix pass" comment feature: three module-level helper functions (`reportInvalidStructuredReview`, `reportChecksPermissionDenied`, `reportInvalidReviewSelection`) post terminal PR comments but, being defined outside `postPushReviewStep`'s closure, have no access to `rejectedCommentBlock()` — and two of them are reachable mid-run (iteration ≥2) after an earlier fix pass already recorded a rejection, so that terminal comment silently omits it, contradicting the PR's own stated intent that every terminal comment carries accumulated rejections. The two items both prior automated reviews already flagged as non-blocking (the raw SHA-256 findingKey in the comment, and the un-amended ADR 028) remain unaddressed in this commit and are restated here as minor.

No blocking issues found in the current diff; the three findings above are all minor/non-blocking.

### Findings

- **[minor]** (src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts:1902): The new "Rejected by the fix pass" block (rejectedCommentBlock(), a closure-local function inside postPushReviewStep) is appended to all 13 postPrComment call sites inside the main step closure, but three earlier-defined, module-level helper functions — reportInvalidStructuredReview (line ~1902, posts the invalid_review terminal comment), reportChecksPermissionDenied (line ~1939, posts the checks_permission_denied terminal comment), and reportInvalidReviewSelection (~line 1576) — have no access to rejectedFindingsByKey/rejectedCommentBlock because they only take ghSpawn/prNumber/iteration, not a reference into the per-run closure. reportChecksPermissionDenied and reportInvalidStructuredReview are both called from inside the per-iteration while loop (lines 2171, 2219, 2292), i.e. reachable on iteration 2+, after an earlier iteration's fix pass already disposed a finding `invalid` and recorded it in rejectedFindingsByKey. Concretely: iteration 1's fix pass dispositions a finding `invalid` (recorded into rejectedFindingsByKey); on iteration 2 the external review check run can no longer be read because the GitHub App's Checks: read grant lapsed mid-run, ciChecksResult.permissionDenied becomes true, and reportChecksPermissionDenied posts the terminal "checks_permission_denied" comment with no "Rejected by the fix pass" section, even though a rejection was recorded earlier in the same run — contradicting docs/review-fix-rail.md's claim that "Fix-pass comments and approved and unapproved terminal PR comments list rejections and their reasons."
- **[minor]** (src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts:2026): rejectedCommentBlock() renders the raw 64-character SHA-256 findingKey to a human reader instead of a human-readable source/path/line/reason the way the analogous renderDeferredFindingsComment (src/runner-callback.ts) does for follow-up dispositions. A maintainer reading the terminal PR comment's "Rejected by the fix pass" section expecting to see which finding (file/line/source) was rejected and why instead sees only an opaque hex key with the reason, making it hard to correlate without cross-referencing the earlier review comment. Still present after the fix-pass commit; both prior automated reviews flagged this as intentional/non-blocking, but it remains a real readability gap in the new feature's primary PR-facing surface.
- **[minor]** (docs/adr/028-the-fixing-agent-dispositions-each-finding-and-may-defer-out-of-scope-ones.md): This PR changes the documented policy for an `invalid` disposition (previously "stays gating so the next review decides", now permanently closes the finding via a new `rejected` ledger status) and docs/review-fix-rail.md cites "ADR 028 decision 4" for the new rule, but ADR 028's decision 4 text itself was not amended and still only covers `follow-up`/`deferred`. This ADR already has an `Amendment (2026-10-28)` section for an equivalent-scope extension of the `deferred` rule; the same pattern was not followed here, so a future reader opening ADR 028 decision 4 to understand why `rejected` findings are treated like `deferred` ones in LateExternalReview's fail-closed check will find no mention of `rejected`/`invalid` and have to reverse-engineer the rule from review-fix-rail.md and the code instead. Flagged by both prior automated reviews as non-blocking, and still unaddressed in the fix-pass commit.
